{{nihongo|'''Kehi Shrine'''|氣比神宮|Kehi Jingū}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in the Akebono-chō neighborhood of the city of {{ill|Tsuruga, Fukui|en|Tsuruga, Fukui|qid=Q847581|lt=Tsuruga}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|en|Fukui Prefecture|qid=Q133879|lt=Fukui Prefecture}}, {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|qid=Q17|lt=Japan}}. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of former {{ill|Echizen Province|en|Echizen Province|qid=Q1047144|lt=Echizen Province}}. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on September 4.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}}</ref>  The shrine is considered the chief guardian shrine of the {{ill|Hokuriku region|en|Hokuriku region|qid=Q381025|lt=Hokuriku region}}.

==Enshrined ''kami''==
The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Kehi Jingū are:
*{{nihongo|'''Izasawake-no-mikoto'''|伊奢沙別命}}, the semi-legendary Prince Tsunuga Arashito, who traveled from his home in {{ill|Silla|en|Silla|qid=Q28456|lt=Silla}} to Tsuruga during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ar|الإمبراطور سوجين|arz|الامبراطور سوجين|azb|سوجین (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Sujin|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سوجین|cs|Sudžin|de|Sujin|el|Αυτοκράτορας Σουτζίν|es|Sujin Tennō|fa|امپراتور سوجین|fr|Sujin|hr|Sujin|id|Kaisar Sujin|it|Sujin|ja|崇神天皇|ka|სუძინი|ko|스진 천황|ms|Maharaja Sujin|nl|Sujin|pl|Sujin|pt|Sujin|ru|Император Судзин|sh|Car Sujin|simple|Emperor Sujin|sl|Cesar Sudžin|sr|Суџин|sv|Sujin|th|จักรพรรดิซูจิง|tl|Emperador Sujin|tr|Sujin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Судзін|uz|Imperator Sujin|vi|Thiên hoàng Sujin|yo|Emperor Sujin|zh|崇神天皇|zh_classical|崇神天皇|zh_min_nan|Suzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|崇神天皇|qid=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}. According to the ''Nihon Shoki'' he had horns coming from his head; the area was named “Tsunuga,” written, literally, “horn-deer,” and over time it became “Tsuruga.”
*{{nihongo|'''{{ill|Emperor Chūai|en|Emperor Chūai|qid=Q179971|lt=Emperor Chūai}}'''|仲哀天皇|Chūai-tennō}}, the semi-legendary 14th Emperor of Japan
*{{nihongo|'''{{ill|Empress Jingū|ar|الإمبراطورة جينغو|arz|الامبراطوره جينجو|az|Cinqu|bcl|Empress Jingū|ca|Jingu|cs|Džingú|de|Jingū|es|Jingū|eu|Jingū enperatriza|fa|امپراتریس جینگو|fr|Jingū|hr|Jingū (japanska carica)|hu|Dzsingú japán császárnő|id|Permaisuri Jingū|it|Jingū|ja|神功皇后|ka|ძინგუ|ko|진구 황후|nl|Jingu|pl|Jingū|pt|Jingu|ru|Императрица Дзингу|sh|Carica Jingū|si|ජින්ගූ අධිරාජිනිය|simple|Empress Jingū|sl|Cesarica Džingu|sv|Jingu Kogo|te|రాణి జింగూ|th|จักรพรรดินีจิงงู|tl|Emperatris Jingū|tr|Jingū (imparatoriçe)|uk|Імператриця Дзінґу|uz|Imperator Jingū|vi|Thiên hoàng Jingū|zh|神功皇后|zh_min_nan|Sîn-kong Hông-hō͘|zh_yue|神功皇后|qid=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}}'''|神功皇后|Jingū-kōgō}}, consort of Emperor Chūai
*{{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}}'''|ヤマトタケルノミコト|Yamato Takeru no Mikoto}}
*{{nihongo|'''Tama-hime no mikoto'''|玉姫命|}}, the daughter of Empress Jingū
*{{nihongo|'''{{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ōjin}}'''|応神天皇|Ōjin-tennō}}, the 15th Emperor of Japan

==History==
The Kehi Jingū is located in the northeastern part of Tsuruga city in the central part of Fukui prefecture. Tsuruga has a good natural port, and was the gateway between the [[:en:Kinai region|Kinai region]] and the {{ill|Korea|en|Korea|qid=Q18097|lt=Korea}} and Asian continent since ancient times. Because of its location, the shine was given particular importance by the imperial court, and is mentioned frequently in ancient chronicles such as the "[[Kojiki]]" and "[[Nihon Shoki]]", especially in connection to events connected with the semi-legendary {{ill|Emperor Chūai|en|Emperor Chūai|qid=Q179971|lt=Emperor Chūai}}, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ar|الإمبراطورة جينغو|arz|الامبراطوره The actual foundation of the shrine predates written history, and its first mention in national chronicles is from around 692 AD during the reign of [[:en:Empress Jito|Empress Jito]]. During the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, imperial messengers were frequently dispatched to the shrine, and its Ranking within the court hierarchy steadily rose, as described in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'', ''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'', ''{{ill|Nihon Kiryaku|ar|نيهون غيرياكو|fr|Nihon kiryaku|ja|日本紀略|ko|일본기략|sl|Nihon kirjaku|zh|日本紀略|qid=Q1053542|lt=Nihon Kiryaku}}'' and other historical sources. In the 927 ''[[Engishiki]]'', it is listed as a ''myōjin taisha'' and by the end of the Heian period was the ''ichinomiya'' of the province. In the Heian and {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|qid=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period}}, the shrine commanded vast estates extending from Echizen to {{ill|Echigo Province|be|Этыго (правінцыя)|ckb|پارێزگای ئێچیگۆ|cs|Provincie Ečigo|de|Provinz Echigo|es|Provincia de Echigo|fa|ولایت اچیگو|fr|Province d'Echigo|gl|Provincia de Echigo|id|Provinsi Echigo|it|Echigo|ja|越後国|ko|에치고국|lt|Ečigo žemė|nl|Echigo (provincie)|pt|Província de Echigo|ru|Этиго (провинция)|simple|Echigo Province|sk|Ečigo (provincia)|sr|Провинција Ечиго|tr|Echigo (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Етіґо|zh|越後國|zh_min_nan|Etigo-kok|zh_yue|越後國|qid=Q666514|lt=Echigo}} and {{ill|Sado Province|cs|Provincie Sado|de|Provinz Sado|es|Provincia de Sado|fa|ولایت سادو|fr|Province de Sado|id|Provinsi Sado|it|Sado (provincia)|ja|佐渡国|ko|사도국|lt|Sado žemė|nl|Sado (provincie)|pt|Província de Sado|ru|Садо (провинция)|simple|Sado Province|sk|Sado (provincia)|sr|Провинција Садо|tr|Sado (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Садо|zh|佐渡國|zh_min_nan|Sado-kok|zh_yue|佐渡國|qid=Q1063844|lt=Sado Province}}. The shrine sided with the [[Southern Court]] in the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|en|Nanboku-chō period|qid=Q264012|lt=Nanboku-chō period}}, and even after defeat by the {{ill|Northern Court|en|Northern Court|qid=Q1201819|lt=Northern Court}}, still commanded territory with a ''{{ill|Kokudaka|es|Kokudaka|fa|ککوداکا|ff|Kokudaka|fr|Kokudaka|it|Kokudaka|ja|石高|ko|석고 (일본사)|ms|Kokudaka|pt|Kokudaka|zh|石高|qid=Q909302|lt=Kokudaka}}'' of 240,000 ''{{ill|Koku|en|Koku|qid=Q855048|lt=Koku}}''. The shrine supported the {{ill|Asakura clan|ca|Clan Asakura|cs|Klan Asakura|de|Asakura (Klan)|eo|Asakura (klano)|es|Clan Asakura|fa|خاندان آساکورا|fi|Asakura-klaani|fr|Clan Asakura|it|Clan Asakura|ja|朝倉氏|ko|아사쿠라씨|nl|Asakura (familie)|pl|Asakura (ród)|pt|Clã Asakura|ru|Асакура (род)|tr|Asakura boyu|uk|Рід Асакура|vi|Gia tộc Asakura|zh|朝倉氏|qid=Q1772267|lt=Asakura clan}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ar|فترة سينغوكو|arz|فتره سينجوكو|be|Перыяд Сэнгоку|bg|Сенгоку|bn|সেনগোকু যুগ|bo|སེན་གོའི་དུས་མཚམས་|ca|Període Sengoku|ckb|سەردەمی سێنگۆکو|cs|Období Sengoku|de|Sengoku-Zeit|eo|Epoko Sengoku|es|Período Sengoku|et|Sengoku ajastu|eu|Sengoku aroa|fa|دوره سنگوکو|fi|Sengoku-kausi|fr|Époque Sengoku|ga|Tréimhse Sengoku|glk|سنگؤکۊ زمات|he|תקופת סנגוקו|hu|Hadakozó fejedelemségek kora (Japán)|id|Zaman Sengoku|is|Sengoku-öldin|it|Periodo Sengoku|ja|戦国時代 (日本)|ka|სენგოკუს პერიოდი|kk|Сэнгоку дәуірі|ko|센고쿠 시대|lt|Sengoku laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Sengoku|nl|Sengokuperiode|no|Sengoku-perioden|pl|Sengoku (okres)|pt|Período Sengoku|ro|Perioada Sengoku|ru|Период Сэнгоку|sh|Sengoku razdoblje|simple|Sengoku period|sk|Obdobie Sengoku|sq|Periudha Sengoku|sr|Сенгоку период|sv|Sengoku|th|ยุคเซ็งโงกุ|tl|Panahong Sengoku|tr|Sengoku Dönemi|uk|Період Сенґоку|ur|سینگوکو دور|uz|Sengoku davri|vi|Thời kỳ Chiến Quốc (Nhật Bản)|wuu|战国时代（日本）|zh|战国时代 (日本)|zh_min_nan|Sengoku sî-tāi|zh_yue|戰國時代 (日本)|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku period}} and was thus largely destroyed by the forces of {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|en|Oda Nobunaga|qid=Q171411|lt=Oda Nobunaga}}. In the early [[:en:Edo Period|Edo Period]], the shrine's restored with a  very modest 100 ''koku'' by {{ill|Yūki Hideyasu|arz|يوكى هيدياسو|eo|Yuki Hideyasu|fa|یوکی هیده‌یاسو|fr|Yūki Hideyasu|it|Yūki Hideyasu|ja|結城秀康|ko|유키 히데야스|pt|Yūki Hideyasu|ru|Юки Хидэясу|uk|Юкі Хідеясу|zh|結城秀康|qid=Q1130929|lt=Yūki Hideyasu}} in 1604. It also received donation from {{ill|Tokugawa Iemitsu|ar|توكوغاوا إيميتسو|br|Tokugawa Iemitsu|ca|Tokugawa Iemitsu|cs|Iemicu Tokugawa|de|Tokugawa Iemitsu|es|Tokugawa Iemitsu|eu|Tokugawa Iemitsu|fa|توکوگاوا ایه‌میتسو|fi|Tokugawa Iemitsu|fr|Tokugawa Iemitsu|hak|Tokugawa Iemitsu|hu|Tokugava Iemicu|id|Tokugawa Iemitsu|is|Tokugawa Iemitsu|it|Tokugawa Iemitsu|ja|徳川家光|ko|도쿠가와 이에미쓰|ms|Tokugawa Iemitsu|nl|Tokugawa Iemitsu|no|Tokugawa Iemitsu|pl|Iemitsu Tokugawa|pt|Tokugawa Iemitsu|ru|Токугава Иэмицу|sk|Iemicu Tokugawa|sr|Токугава Јемицу|sv|Tokugawa Iemitsu|th|โทกูงาวะ อิเอมิตสึ|tr|Tokugawa Iemitsu|uk|Токуґава Ієміцу|vi|Tokugawa Iemitsu|wuu|德川家光|zh|德川家光|zh_min_nan|Tokugawa Iemitu|zh_yue|德川家光|qid=Q314481|lt=Tokugawa Iemitsu}} and by the various ''[[:en:Daimyō|Daimyō]]'' of {{ill|Ōno Domain|fa|قلمرو اونو|fr|Domaine d'Ōno|ja|大野藩|ru|Оно (княжество)|zh|大野藩|qid=Q10863325|lt=Ōno Domain}}, but never regained its former prosperity. In September of 1689, Kehi Jingu Shrine was visited by the famous poet [[:en:Matsuo Basho|Matsuo Basho]], and his visit is still commemorated with a statue and a stone monument inscribed with his {{ill|Haiku|af|Haikoe|als|Haiku|ar|هايكو|as|হাইকু|ast|Haiku|awa|हाइकु|az|Hayku|ba|Хайку|bar|Haiku|be|Хайку|be_x_old|Хайку|bg|Хайку|bi|Haiku|bn|হাইকু|bo|ཧའི་གུ།|br|Haiku|ca|Haiku|cbk_zam|Haiku|ckb|ھایکوو|cs|Haiku|cu|Хаикоу|cy|Haiku|da|Haiku|de|Haiku|el|Χαϊκού|eo|Hajko|es|Haiku|et|Haiku|eu|Haiku|fa|هایکو|fi|Haiku|fiu_vro|Haiku|fr|Haïku|fy|Haikû|ga|Haiku|gan|俳句|gl|Haiku|gn|Haiku|gu|હાઈકુ|he|הייקו|hi|हाइकु|hr|Haiku|hu|Haiku|hy|Հոքու|ia|Haiku|id|Haiku|ie|Haiku|io|Haikuo|is|Hæka|it|Haiku|ja|俳句|jam|Aikuu|ka|ჰაიკუ|ko|하이쿠|ku|Haikû|ky|Хайку|la|Haicu|lb|Haiku|lfn|Haicu|li|Haiku|ln|Haiku|lt|Haiku|lv|Haiku|mk|Хаику|ml|ഹൈക്കു|mn|Хайкү|ms|Haiku|my|ဟိုက်ခု|nds_nl|Haiku|ne|हाइकु|nl|Haiku (dichtvorm)|nn|Haiku|no|Haiku|nrm|Haiku|or|ହାଇକୁ|pa|ਹਾਇਕੂ|pam|Haiku|pap|Haiku|pcd|Haïku|pl|Haiku|pms|Haiku|pnb|ہائیکو|ps|هايکو|pt|Haiku|ro|Haiku|ru|Хайку|sco|Haiku|sd|ھائيڪو|sh|Haiku|simple|Haiku|sk|Haiku|sl|Haiku|sq|Haiku|sr|Хаику|su|Haiku|sv|Haiku|sw|Haiku|ta|ஐக்கூ|te|హైకూ|tg|Ҳойку|th|ไฮกุ|tl|Haiku|tr|Haiku|tt|Хайку|uk|Хайку|ur|ہائیکو|vi|Haiku|wa|Haycou|wuu|俳句|zh|俳句|zh_classical|俳句|zh_yue|俳句|qid=Q37707|lt=Haiku}}.<ref name="Yoshiki">{{cite book |last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese}}</ref>

During the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} era of {{ill|State Shinto|bn|রাষ্ট্রীয় শিন্তৌ|de|Staats-Shintō|es|Sintoísmo estatal|fa|شینتوی حکومتی|fr|Shintoïsme d'État|id|Shinto Negara|ja|国家神道|ko|국가신토|no|Statsshinto|pt|Xintoísmo estatal|ru|Государственный синтоизм|simple|State Shinto|tr|Devlet Şintoizmi|vi|Thần đạo Quốc gia|zh|国家神道|qid=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto}}, the shrine was rated as a{{nihongo|Imperial shrine, 1st Rank |官幣大社|Kanpei Taisha}} under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines]]<ref>Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125.</ref>

The shrine was mostly destroyed in 1945, during the [[Bombing of Tsuruga in World War II]] by American forces, and its {{ill|National Treasure (Japan)|en|National Treasure (Japan)|qid=Q1139795|lt=National Treasure}} ''[[Honden]]'' built in the Edo period by Yūki Hideyasu burned down. One surviving structure is the shrine's 11-meter-tall [[torii]] gate, which was built in 1902 and which is registered as a National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|de|Wichtiges Kulturgut Japans|es|Bien Cultural Importante de Japón|fi|Japanin tärkeä kulttuuriomaisuus|fr|Bien culturel important|id|Properti Kebudayaan Penting (Jepang)|it|Bene culturale importante (Giappone)|ja|重要文化財|ko|일본의 중요문화재|ro|Patrimoniu cultural important al Japoniei|simple|Important Cultural Properties of Japan|th|ทรัพย์สินทางวัฒนธรรมที่สำคัญ (ญี่ปุ่น)|tr|Önemli Kültürel Varlık (Japonya)|uk|Важливі культурні пам'ятки Японії|zh|重要文化財|qid=Q1188622|lt=[Important Cultural Property}}. It is the third largest wooden torii gate in Japan, alongside {{ill|Nara (city)|af|Nara, Nara|an|Nara|ar|نارا (مدينة)|arz|نارا|az|Nara (şəhər)|azb|نارا (ژاپن)|ba|Нара (ҡала)|ban|Nara, Nara|be|Нара (горад)|bg|Нара|ca|Nara (Japó)|ce|Нара (гӀала)|ceb|Nara-shi (distrito)|cs|Nara|cy|Nara|de|Nara|el|Νάρα|eo|Nara|es|Nara (Nara)|et|Nara|eu|Nara|fa|نارا (شهر)|fi|Nara|fr|Nara|ga|Nara|gl|Nara|hak|Nai-liòng-sṳ|he|נארה|hr|Nara (Japan)|hu|Nara (Japán)|hy|Նարա (քաղաք)|id|Nara, Nara|io|Nara|it|Nara|ja|奈良市|ka|ნარა (ქალაქი)|ko|나라시|ky|Нара|la|Nara|lt|Nara (Japonija)|lv|Nara|mad|Nara, Nara|min|Nara, Nara|mk|Нара (Јапонија)|mn|Нара|ms|Nara, Nara|mzn|نارا|nl|Nara (stad)|no|Nara (by)|pl|Nara (miasto w Japonii)|pt|Nara (cidade)|ro|Nara|ru|Нара (город)|sc|Nara|sd|نارا (شهر)|sh|Nara, Nara|si|නාරා, නාරා|simple|Nara, Nara|sk|Nara (Nara)|sl|Nara (mesto)|sr|Нара|sv|Nara, Nara|sw|Nara, Nara|szl|Nara (mjasto we Japůńiji)|tg|Нара|th|นาระ (เมือง)|tl|Lungsod ng Nara|tok|ma tomo Nala|tr|Nara|tt|Нара (шәһәр)|uk|Нара|ur|نارا، نارا|uz|Nara|vi|Nara (thành phố)|war|Nara (syudad)|wuu|奈良市|zh|奈良市|zh_classical|奈良市|zh_min_nan|Nara-chhī|zh_yue|奈良市|qid=Q169134|lt=Nara}}’s [[Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Taisha]] Shrine and {{ill|Hiroshima|en|Hiroshima|qid=Q34664|lt=Hiroshima}}’s [[Itsukushima Shrine]].<ref name="Yoshiki"/>

The shrine is located a 15-minute walk from {{ill|Tsuruga Station|en|Tsuruga Station|qid=Q5364670|lt=Tsuruga Station}}on the {{ill|West Japan Railway Company|en|West Japan Railway Company|qid=Q502125|lt=West Japan Railway Company}} {{ill|Hokuriku Main Line|en|Hokuriku Main Line|qid=Q1318747|lt=Hokuriku Main Line}}.<ref name="Okada">{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}}</ref>

==Cultural Properties==
===Important Cultural Properties===
*{{nihongo|'''Kehi Jingū Ō[[torii]]'''|気比神宮大鳥居||}}, Edo Period, 1645, wooden, painted vermillion. This torii gate has a height of 10.93 meters. The inscription is by Prince [[:en:Arisugawa Takehito|Arisugawa Takehito]].<ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/817|title=気比神宮大鳥居〉|trans-title=Kehi Jingū Ōtorii |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}}</ref>
